To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
inter-organizational Continuous Integration and Delivery is possible, and legal contracts are an important impediment to inter-organizational continuous integration and delivery.

inter-organizational continuous integration and delivery in the automotive ecosystem can be achieved with limited transparency and that the main impediment for this approach is the legal contracts that govern the relationships between the different companies.

(i) transparency is considered positive and not a necessary condition to enable inter-organizational continuous integration and delivery, (ii) legal contracts are a major impediment for inter-company continuous integration and delivery and (iii) information sharing is a major challenge for inter-organisational continuous integration and delivery.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how inter-organizational Continuous Integration and Delivery is enabled in the automotive ecosystem.
the following research question: What is the role of transparency and contracts in inter-organizational Continuous Integration and Delivery?
the question of how to make inter-organizational software development more transparent and how this transparency can help in overcoming the impediments that arise from legal contracts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
inter-organizational contracts are a necessary evil.
inter-organizational continuous integration and delivery in the automotive domain requires transparency but not necessarily full transparency.
transparency is not a necessary condition but is a facilitator for inter-organizatonal CI&D in the context of automotive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the automotive ecosystem is not ready yet for inter-organizable CI&D.
transparency is a necessary condition for information sharing but not a sufficient condition for inter-organization CI&D.

the automotive ecosystem is ready for CI&D, but the contracts that are used to regulate the relationships between the companies in the automotive ecosystem are an impediment to inter-organizational continuous integration and delivery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
transparency and legal contracts are two key factors for the successful implementation of inter-organizational software development practices.
the current legal frameworks in the automotive domain are a major impediment for the adoption of inter-organizational software development and CI&D practices.
the automotive domain is a good case study for understanding the impact of legal contracts on inter-organizational software engineering.
